record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, .... For every integer m ≥ 1, must the even-index ratio λ₂ₘ/λₘ always satisfy λ₂ₘ/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)_{n-ball}?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ and all m ≥ 1 show that λ₂ₘ/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)|n-ball.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $0 < \lambda_1(\Omega) \le \lambda_2(\Omega) \le \lambda_3(\Omega) \le \cdots$ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e., the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u \in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$. Let $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote any ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (the ratio below is scale-invariant), and write
$$R_n := \frac{\lambda_2(B)}{\lambda_1(B)} = \frac{j_{n/2,1}^2}{j_{n/2-1,1}^2},$$
where $j_{\nu,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and every integer $m \ge 1$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{2m}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)} \le R_n.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The classical PPW conjecture (case m=1) was solved by Ashbaugh and Benguria in the 1990s, but its generalization to ratios λ_{2m}/λ_m for all m ≥ 1 remains an open conjecture. Recent works (e.g., on Ashbaugh–Benguria's conjecture about lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues) make partial progress but do not establish the general bound.

status_evidence.title: On Ashbaugh-Benguria's Conjecture about Lower Order Dirichlet Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: An isoperimetric inequality for lower order eigenvalues ... makes progress toward proving a conjecture by Ashbaugh-Benguria regarding ratios of higher-order Dirichlet eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: The higher-order ratio conjecture remains an open problem with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Rayleigh-Faber-Krahn inequality - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: λ₂(Ω)/λ₁(Ω) ≤ j²_{n/2,1}/j²_{n/2-1,1}, with equality if and only if Ω is a ball (Ashbaugh-Benguria).
status_evidence.claim: The m=1 case is the resolved PPW inequality; higher m is the natural extension.
